text: Which of the following statements about shadow AI is CORRECT?

options.text: Shadow AI enforces compliance with organizational data policies and general AI regulations.
Shadow AI eliminates the need for clear licensing agreements in AI tools.
Shadow AI reduces the risk of intellectual property disputes.
Shadow AI may lead to unauthorized accesses to sensitive information.

explanation: Shadow AI is the use of AI tools without organizational approval or oversight. It can lead to unauthorized access to or leakage of sensitive information, violates data and licensing policies, and increases IP risks.

text: What is a key aspect to consider when defining a Generative AI strategy for software testing?

options.text: Prepare training programs designed to ensure that team members obtain certifications specific to each LLM they use.
Select LLMs that can be integrated appropriately with existing test environments and test tools.
Ensure that as much input data as possible is available to increase the likelihood of obtaining effective LLM outputs.
Collect standard supervised machine learning metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of LLM outputs.

explanation: A GenAI strategy should select LLMs that integrate with existing test environments and tools. Per-LLM certifications, maximal input data and standard supervised ML metrics are not key aspects.

text: Which of the following statements BEST describes one of the key criteria to select an appropriate LLM for specific test tasks within a test organization?

options.text: A key selection criterion involves evaluating the LLM’s performance for the test tasks against the publicly available benchmarks for LLMs in code generation.
A key selection criterion involves evaluating recurring costs such as those associated with the computational resources required to run the LLM.
A key selection criterion involves evaluating the LLM against the publicly available community benchmarks to ensure full compatibility with them.
A key selection criterion involves evaluating recurring costs such as those associated with a proof of concept aimed at demonstrating the suitability of an LLM for the test tasks.

explanation: Recurring costs (such as the compute resources needed to run the LLM) are a key selection criterion. Public benchmarks can inform but do not prove fit for specific test tasks, and proof-of-concept costs are not recurring costs.

text: What are the key phases in the adoption of Generative AI in a test organization?

options.text: Discovery, initiation and usage definition, utilization and iteration
Awareness, usage prioritization, performance monitoring
Planning, experimentation, evaluation and refinement
Training, testing, implementation, and scaling

explanation: The syllabus phases are discovery, initiation and usage definition, and utilization and iteration. The other options are generic or invented sequences.

text: Which of the following options BEST refers to an example of knowledge and/or skills required for testers to work effectively with LLMs in test processes?

options.text: Mastering techniques specifically aimed at preventing LLMs from hallucinating and incurring reasoning errors when performing specific test tasks.
Selecting and implementing suitable test automation approaches, such as keyword-driven test automation, for automating test processes.
Choosing the most appropriate LLM based on criteria such as its capability to be adapted or customized to perform specific test tasks.
Ensuring the validation and test data used in the development of the LLMS are of the highest quality.

explanation: Choosing the right LLM based on criteria such as adaptability to specific test tasks is a skill testers need. Preventing hallucinations is a general risk mitigation, keyword-driven automation is not LLM-specific, and quality of LLM development data is not a tester skill.

text: What is the BEST approach for cultivating skills within test teams to specifically support the adoption of Generative AI?

options.text: Rely mainly on external expert courses with hands-on practice, aiming to integrate AI into all daily test tasks at once.
Encourage independent experimentation with various LLMs without following a structured process.
Adopt a hands-on, gradual learning process supported by guided exercises, peer learning, and knowledge-sharing communities.
Rely mainly on theoretical courses from external experts, aiming to gradually integrate AI into daily test tasks in line with actual learning.

explanation: Skills are best built gradually with hands-on practice, guided exercises, peer learning and knowledge-sharing communities. Unstructured experimentation, all-at-once adoption and theory-only courses are less effective.

text: Which of the following answers BEST describes how the roles and responsibilities of testers and test managers within a test organization are impacted by the adoption of Generative AI for software testing?

options.text: Testers shift their focus from manually designing test cases to guiding and verifying AI-generated testware.
Test managers shift their focus from managing test projects to understanding the inner working of Generative AI technologies.
Testers shift their focus from manually designing test cases to overseeing AI-based test processes.
Test managers shift their focus from relying on people to relying solely on Generative AI to boost productivity in test tasks.

explanation: Testers shift from manually designing test cases to guiding and verifying AI-generated testware, which keeps human responsibility for quality. "Overseeing AI-based processes" overstates the shift, and test managers still manage projects and do not rely solely on GenAI.

text: When an organization begins adopting Generative AI tools across testing teams without official IT approval or security review (known as "Shadow AI"), what is the most appropriate first governance step?

options.text: Ban all computers in the testing department immediately.
Identify the usage, assess the associated security and compliance risks, and establish a clear GenAI adoption roadmap and policy.
Assume the AI output is always bug-free and scale it to production deployment.
Dismiss all human testers to cut costs.

explanation: Governance requires discovering "Shadow AI," evaluating risks (privacy, reliability), and implementing a structured change management and enablement roadmap.

text: A team compares candidate LLMs for an internal testing assistant. Which evaluation is most relevant?

options.text: Task performance, integration, privacy and recurring cost
Brand popularity alone
The longest model name
Number of marketing videos

explanation: Model selection should reflect the actual task, constraints, integration, and cost.

text: Which sequence best represents the syllabus adoption roadmap?

options.text: Discovery; initiation and usage definition; utilization and iteration
Deployment; deletion; replacement
Training; ignoring feedback; shutdown
Purchase; production; no evaluation

explanation: The syllabus describes discovery, initiation and usage definition, and utilization and iteration.

text: What is a sustainable way to build GenAI capability in a testing team?

options.text: Combine training, practical experimentation and shared learning
Give everyone unrestricted access without guidance
Measure success only by prompts written
Avoid peer review

explanation: Capability building requires skills development and practical organizational learning.

text: How is the risk of using copyrighted data without proper authorization categorized when using shadow AI?

options.text: Information security weakness
Data privacy weakness
Compliance issues
Vague intellectual property

explanation: Shadow AI tools may have unclear licensing agreements and may use copyrighted data without proper authorization — a vague intellectual property risk.

text: Why is high-quality input data important when implementing an LLM-powered testing approach?

options.text: It will be faster with good data that produces fewer errors
It will produce reliable results
It will allow the largest possible data set to be built
It will ensure access is protected and limited to only the correct users

explanation: LLM output quality depends on input quality; high-quality input data produces reliable results.

text: You are working to convince your manager that a GenAI tool would be helpful in generating test reports. The manager feels that hiring interns to write the test reports would be faster than incorporating a new tool. You are sure the tool will write the reports faster and more accurately, freeing critical testing time. What is an important capability of the LLM that you should evaluate to be sure it will prove you right?

options.text: Model performance
Fine-tuning potential
Direct cost
Community and support

explanation: Your claim is about speed and accuracy, so you must verify the model performs efficiently and accurately on report generation tasks.

text: What is the first key phase when adopting GenAI into the test organization?

options.text: Discovery
Initiation and Training
Usage Definition
Exploitation and Iteration

explanation: Adoption starts with Discovery, followed by initiation and usage definition, then exploitation and iteration.

text: Why does a tester need to understand "prompt engineering" in order to work effectively with GenAI?

options.text: Because they will have a better grasp of the internal layers of the neural network
Because they need to understand what user prompts will need to be tested and the relative risk of each
Because they will be asked to generate new user prompts based on the AI-designed UI
Because they will need to design and refine the input prompts to guide the LLM

explanation: Prompt engineering is the skill of designing and refining input prompts to guide the LLM toward useful output.

text: When conducting GenAI training meetings with the testing team, what is an important learning method?

options.text: Discussing challenges and their resolutions
Highlighting erroneous prompts used within the team
Processing AI outputs to better analyze manual testing gaps
Promoting the use of AI methods and nominating an "AI champion of the week"

explanation: A key method highlighted in the syllabus is discussing challenges and their resolutions as a team. The other options might be informative but are not the highlighted method.

text: Who is usually responsible for ensuring that test teams maintain both traditional testing competencies and AI literacy?

options.text: Each tester
The senior testers
The test manager
The AI master

explanation: The test manager usually ensures the team as a whole has these capabilities; individuals remain responsible for keeping their own skills current.

text: An audit finds that nobody can tell which test cases were AI-generated and that generated testware is not reviewed. Which elements of the GenAI strategy are missing?

options.text: Larger context windows.
Cheaper models.
Transparency obligations and quality gates.
Fine-tuning and RAG.

explanation: Process guidelines should include transparency obligations (what was generated using GenAI) and quality gates with review of generated testware.

text: Which statement about the phases of GenAI adoption is CORRECT?

options.text: Fear of job displacement is out of scope.
Phases can run in parallel for different use cases, and early concerns such as fear of job displacement should be addressed.
All use cases must complete Discovery before any starts Initiation.
Utilization and iteration come before Discovery.

explanation: Phases can run in parallel (e.g. report analysis may be ahead of test automation), and concerns like job displacement must be addressed to protect adoption and morale.

text: What is a prompt pattern?

options.text: A model weight file.
A tokenization rule.
A type of attack vector.
A reusable template for crafting effective prompts that guides GenAI toward consistent, reliable outputs.

explanation: Prompt patterns are shared via libraries and communities of practice as part of building GenAI capability.
